headline: Singapore's central bank left its exchange-rate policy unchanged on Wednesday, expecting the AI boom and the energy squeeze to ease in 2027, as the economy grew 5.4% in the third quarter.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: the central bank's statement and growth figures were read in full; the AI link is the bank's forecast that AI activity eases in 2027.
importance_line: What changed is that a central bank that had been tightening has paused because it sees AI-driven growth fading in 2027, which matters first to Singapore households and firms facing slightly elevated prices, then to currency and bond traders, then to AI-linked exporters, and the doubt is that the bank itself says inflation risks lean upward.
summary: Bloomberg reports that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), which steers policy through the exchange rate rather than interest rates, unexpectedly kept the slope, width and centre of its currency policy band unchanged on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026, its first pause after tightening in April and July, because it expects both the global energy crunch and the AI boom to ease in 2027. AsiaOne adds that all ten analysts polled by Reuters had expected a tightening, that Singapore's economy grew 5.4% in the third quarter from a year earlier, down from 6.2% in the second, and that MAS expects steady growth until AI-related activity eases in the second half of 2027, with risks to inflation "tilted to the upside".
notes: Bloomberg is paywalled after two paragraphs; figures from AsiaOne's full report of the MAS statement.
